findings.finding: The producer's headline says the selection-bias control (keys fixed per cell on repeat 0, scored on repeats 1-2) shows 'the same pattern, 0.75-1.28x'. The range recomputes exactly (0.7518-1.2843), but the control's protocol decisions differ from the primary rule in 3 of 9 cells: 2^24 T = 16384 unranked (0.752 [0.655, 1.211]), 2^28 T = 1024 unranked (0.975 [0.884, 1.137]) and 2^32 T = 1024 unranked (1.096 [0.972, 1.351]). The control therefore supports 'faster' in 2 of 3 cells at 2^24, none at 2^28 and 'slower' in 2 of 3 at 2^32. Validator leave-one-repeat-out diagnostic: 32 of 36 ratios below 1 at 2^24, 2 of 36 at 2^32, and 7 of 12 at 2^28 T = 1024.

'A native operation 0.005-0.009 GAE' is canon_hash_ns / padd_ns, and canon_hash_ns times a canonicalisation plus one hash of x, which the harness counts as TWO native operations (rhodpu's canon closure calls f.native() twice per generated point). Per counted native operation the measured price is 0.0025-0.0047 GAE; the step-index loop is 0.0024-0.0057 GAE, not 0.005-0.009 as RESULTS ('or a step index') says. Both include the loop overhead (loop baseline 0.61-0.88 ns, 0.0026-0.0041 GAE). The conclusion that native work is nearly free (h_native about 0) is unaffected.

findings.finding: Validator timing on the same host, the same bit-identical binary, pinned to CPU 2, with the producer's per-configuration keys (selected on the producer's medians, scored on new timings). Round 1 (3 repeats, part A all 36 configurations + part B one nonce-drawn configuration per cell x 17 keys): 6 of 9 decisions reproduced; 2^24 T = 16384 (0.911 [0.811, 1.009]), 2^28 T = 1024 (0.991 [0.970, 1.043]) and 2^32 T = 1024 (1.072 [0.954, 1.109]) unranked: the three cells where the producer's fixed-key control is also unranked. Round 2 (5 repeats, added after round 1 and reported separately): 8 of 9 (2^28 T = 1024 unranked, 0.943 [0.924, 1.140]). Pooled (8 repeats per key): 9 of 9 decisions reproduced; 2^24 0.768-0.845 (12 of 12 configurations below 1), 2^28 0.976-1.016 (T = 1024 0.980 [0.959, 0.999], faster by a hair), 2^32 1.107-1.216 (12 of 12 above 1). Every producer cell interval overlaps the pooled validator interval. Per-configuration ratios differ between sessions by a median of 5.1% (p90 14%, max 22%), more than the within-session A/A median single-repeat deviation (2.8%) and within the per-cell A/A rep0/rep1 intervals. The 2^24 'faster' and 2^32 'slower' directions reproduce; the 28 b T = 1024 magnitude does not (0.93 vs 0.98) and its decision is fragile.

With n = 4 configurations per cell, the protocol's bootstrap 95% interval of the median equals [min, max] of the 4 configuration ratios in all 9 cells (a resample has median equal to the maximum with probability 13/256 > 2.5%; the exact bootstrap over all 256 resamples gives the same bounds). A 'faster'/'slower' decision therefore means all 4 configurations on one side of 1 (two-sided sign-test p = 0.125 for one cell); the '95%' label is nominal. The size-level evidence is the strong part: 12 of 12 configurations below 1 at 2^24 and 12 of 12 above 1 at 2^32 in the producer's data (two-sided sign test p = 0.00049 each), 11 of 12 in validator round 1 and 12 of 12 in round 2 and pooled.

The claim says '12 fresh prime-order Weierstrass curves'. They are the v5 instances W{24,28,32}-{0..3} (first used in v5 with seeds 41 and 42; PROTOCOL.md says so). They are valid (p and n prime, cofactor 1 by Hasse, [n]G = O; n has 24-25, 28-29 and 32-33 bits) and were not tuned on in this study, but they are not fresh. The seed 43 is new.

(a) 'rho2xks (kappa 0.25-0.5) in 7' should be 6, and rhodpu at kappa 0.25 wins 1 (2^32, T = 16384, not mentioned); the distinguished-point rho is fastest in 30 of 36, 29 of them at kappa 0. (b) std lookup at 2^18-2^20 is 0.11-0.42 GAE, not 0.12-0.42 (28 b 'after', 2^18: 0.1145). (c) 'A fast multiplicative hasher is 2-5x cheaper': the std/fast lookup ratio is 1.2-6.1x over the 48 table entries (median 3.8, 10-90% 3.2-4.6). (d) 'although it never won in v5's counted model' is false: the validated, amended v5 RESULTS has rhodpu fastest in 4 of 198 configurations at h = 1 (I = 10 M).

RESULTS labels 'Answer to the v5 question' as interpretation, correctly. Validator price model (not pre-registered; predicted ns = I inv + M mul + S sqr + H lookup(own table size) + N canon_hash/2 at the opcost prices): field operations alone favour the IC at 2^28-2^32 (IC/rho 0.72-0.78); adding the std-HashMap lookup price at each run's own table size predicts 1.14-1.22 at 2^32 ('before' prices; 1.09-1.15 'after') against 1.11-1.29 measured, with lookups about 39-40% of the IC's predicted time and 1-2% of rhodpu's. So 'the IC's large-table lookups cost it the 2^32 cells' is quantitatively consistent; 'lookups miss cache' is not measured (no PMU) and must stay interpretation. At 2^24 the price list predicts 0.85-1.02 against 0.78-0.83 measured, so it does not explain the 2^24 advantage. 'h_native about 0 favours the distinguished-point rho' is consistent (rhodpu's native work is under 1% of its predicted time) but untested as a cause.

findings.severity: pass, with method caveats to disclose
findings.finding: No dead code: the mul, sqr, inv and padd loops are loop-carried dependency chains through black_box; the native and lookup loops accumulate into a value passed to black_box; at param 1.0 every loop runs 4x longer and the counters scale exactly (I 4,000,006, M 26,000,012, S 24,000,009 vs 1,000,006 / 6,500,012 / 6,000,009 at 0.25) while per-operation times stay nonzero and comparable. The padd chain is exactly one affine addition per step: the counters equal the expected I + 2M + S per step plus the two setup multiplications, so there was no doubling and no reset to G. Caveats: lookups are timed as independent probes (memory-level parallelism), not interleaved with dependent field arithmetic as in the harness; probes are 50% inserted keys and 50% uniform in [0, p), so at 24 bits with 2^22-2^24 inserted keys most 'misses' hit (2^24 random keys in [0, 2^24) are about 63% distinct) and the hit mix varies with size and curve; capacity is 2x the key count; single segments can be far off (validator run: one mul segment 28.8 ns against 7.3-7.8, giving I/M 6.0; producer 28 b 'after' padd 294 ns = 1.30x its I + 2M + S). The validator's 7 opcost runs reproduce the producer's ranges apart from that segment: GAE 209-267 ns, I/M 25-34, canonicalisation + hash 0.0055-0.0081 GAE, std lookup 0.047-0.144 (2^10-2^16) and 0.36-0.73 GAE (2^22-2^24).

accepted_results_headline: On one CPU of a 4-vCPU cloud VM (Intel Xeon @ 2.10 GHz; not an isolated lab node, so the seconds are diagnostic), in this harness's implementation (std HashMap with SipHash), 36 configurations (the 12 prime-order Weierstrass curves of the v5 study, group orders about 2^24, 2^28 and 2^32, with a new seed; T = 1024/4096/16384) x 17 run keys x 3 interleaved repeats, every target verified: the fastest of four multi-target index-calculus variants per configuration takes 0.78-0.83x the solve-phase wall time of the fastest of ten multi-target rho runs at 2^24 (faster in all 3 cells; 12 of 12 configurations below 1), 0.93x at 2^28 with T = 1024 (faster under the primary rule, but unranked under the pre-registered fixed-key control and 0.98x in the validator's rerun), is unranked at 2^28 with T = 4096 and 16384, and takes 1.11-1.29x at 2^32 (slower in all 3 cells; 12 of 12 configurations above 1). Each cell decision is a 4-of-4 sign rule (the bootstrap interval of the median of 4 equals their range). The pre-registered fixed-key control (0.75-1.28x) is unranked in one cell at each end (2^24 with T = 16384, 2^32 with T = 1024); an independent pinned rerun with the same keys (8 repeats) reproduces all 9 decisions at 0.77-0.84x (2^24) and 1.11-1.22x (2^32). The IC takes 1.33-1.59x the time of a paired BSGS. Measured prices (opcost microbenchmarks; lookups and native operations timed as independent-iteration loops): one affine addition 214-294 ns, I/M 23-31, a canonicalisation plus one hash of x (two counted native operations) 0.005-0.009 GAE and a step index 0.002-0.006 GAE, a std HashMap lookup 0.04-0.85 GAE at 2^10-2^24 entries.
